explanation: The bug was that the gray-code pointers (wr_ptr_gray and rd_ptr_gray) were not reset when their respective clock domains received a synchronized reset. This caused the full/empty flags to be computed incorrectly immediately after reset, allowing stale data to be read from memory before new data was written. The fix adds explicit reset of wr_ptr_gray in the write block and rd_ptr_gray in the read block when the synchronized reset is asserted. This ensures all pointers and their gray-code representations start from zero after any reset, so the FIFO appears empty and no pre-reset traffic remains.
